title: Principality of Beloozero
capsule: The Principality of Beloozero was a minor Rus' appanage principality centred on the town of Beloozero (modern Belozersk, Vologda Oblast), separated from Rostov as a distinct line around 1238 in the fragmentation following the Mongol invasion. Its rulers were tributaries of the Golden Horde and exercised authority over sparsely populated forest-lake territory northeast of the Sheksna River. By the mid-fourteenth century the principality had passed by inheritance to the Muscovite sphere, and it was definitively absorbed into the Grand Duchy of Moscow under Ivan III around 1486. The 1294–1344 attestation window reflects its period of clearest documentary independence.
attestation: Boundaries from Seshat Cliopatria (Bennett et al., Scientific Data 2025; CC BY 4.0), digitized from standard historical atlases at ~0.07° resolution. Political continuity is attested in Rus' chronicles, but territorial extent is poorly defined and relies on modern reconstructions of appanage boundaries.
